title: Recovering constructibility at a finite boundary
statement:
Let $b:Y\to S$ be proper
between finite-type $k$-schemes, where $k$ is the field of the unit, with the finite coefficients of
[sbc-def-coefficient-conventions].
Let $a:G\hookrightarrow Y$ be open, with closed complement
$i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$, and assume $bi:Z\to S$ is finite.
For $K\in\hyperref[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]{D^+(Y,\Lambda)}$,
suppose $a^*K$ and the direct image
$Rb_*K$ belong to their respective
bounded constructible categories.
Then $K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: The schemes $S,Y,Z$ are Noetherian. Indeed $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, and its spectrum is a one-point affine scheme. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure maps of $S$ and $Y$, and then to the finite morphism $p=bi:Z\to S$. A finite morphism is of finite type since a finite list of module generators of its affine ring algebra also generates that algebra. Thus the Noetherian hypotheses of finite reflection are available. All complexes and functors below have constant coefficients $\Lambda$ on the small etale sites; no adic or pro-etale coefficient category is substituted.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; finite implies finite type directly from affine ring definitions

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] to $a:G\hookrightarrow Y$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ and the given $K\in D^+(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$. With $A=a_!a^*K$ and $C=i_*i^*K$ this gives the distinguished triangle $A\to K\to C\to A[1]$. Here $a^*,i^*$ are the exact constant-coefficient inverse images, not an additional tensor operation: [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies module pullback with inverse image and proves exactness. The recollement statement gives exactness of $i_*$ as well. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] it follows that the termwise closed direct image computes $Ri_*$ on every bounded below complex, so $C\cong Ri_*i^*K$.

source.place: Tag 095L, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; derived.tex Tags 0152 and 015F for passage to the triangle and exact derived functors

proof.text: The sheaf-level constructibility assertion [lem-fin-extension-by-zero] applies to every $\mathcal H^q(a^*K)$, since $Y$ is of finite type over $k$. Exactness of $a_!$ is [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $\mathcal H^q(A)\cong a_!\mathcal H^q(a^*K)$ on a representative complex. Thus these cohomology sheaves are constructible and vanish outside the same finite interval as those of $a^*K$; hence $A\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$. This is a degreewise argument, not an invocation of a sheaf lemma as though it already stated a derived result.

source.place: Proof, paragraph beginning By lem-fin-extension-by-zero; cohomology calculation: homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor

proof.text: Apply $Rb_*$ to the triangle. The general theorem [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] says that the right derived functor of an additive functor on abelian categories with K-injective resolutions carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles. Its hypotheses hold here: use the small-site skeleton of [def-weil-size-convention], and apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to its constant ring sheaf on each small etale site. The unbounded K-injective computation of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] and the bounded below injective representatives of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] identify its restriction to $D^+$ with the $Rb_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]: both compute $K=QI$ as $Q(b_*I)$ and morphisms by the same homotopy classes. Consequently we obtain the distinguished triangle $Rb_*A\to Rb_*K\to Rb_*C\to Rb_*A[1]$ in the ordinary derived category of etale $\Lambda$-modules on $S$. Using $C\cong Ri_*i^*K$, clause (5) of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], which is explicitly for any commutative ring on the small etale site, identifies its third term with $Rp_*i^*K$. None of the narrower coefficient-stage clauses (1)--(4) is used.

Since $b$ is proper between finite-type $k$-schemes, [lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible] applied to $A$ gives $P=Rb_*A\in D^b_c(S,\Lambda)$. Set $Q=Rb_*K$, which is bounded constructible by hypothesis, and $T=Rp_*i^*K$. Choose one interval $[u,v]$ containing the cohomological supports of $P$ and $Q$. The long exact sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] for the preceding triangle contains $\mathcal H^n(Q)\to\mathcal H^n(T)\to\mathcal H^{n+1}(P)$. For $n<u-1$ and for $n>v$ both outer terms vanish, so $T$ is bounded, with support contained in $[u-1,v]$. Now the whole triangle lies in $D^b(S,\Lambda)$; [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory] implies $T\in D^b_c(S,\Lambda)$. Establishing boundedness first is necessary because that cited statement is formulated inside $D^b$, rather than as an assertion about arbitrary cones in $D^+$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: proper direct image and its cone; derived.tex Tag 05RS, lemma-cohomology-homological

proof.text: The inverse image $i^*K$ is in $D^+(Z,\Lambda)$: exactness from [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and the cohomology isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] give $\mathcal H^q(i^*K)\cong i^*\mathcal H^q(K)$, preserving the lower vanishing bound. The morphism $p=bi$ is finite by hypothesis, its source and target are Noetherian by step 1, and $\Lambda$ is finite commutative by the coefficient convention. Therefore [lem-fin-finite-reflects-derived] applies to the bounded constructible $Rp_*i^*K$ of step 5 and yields $i^*K\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: finite reflection; same unit lem-fin-finite-reflects-derived, statement and proof

proof.text: Since $i_*$ is exact by [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement], [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $\mathcal H^q(C)\cong i_*\mathcal H^q(i^*K)$. The right side is constructible by [lem-fin-closed-immersion], whose finite-type hypothesis is on $Y$, and vanishes outside the finite cohomological interval of $i^*K$. Thus $C\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$. To finish, choose an interval containing the supports of $A$ and $C$. In the long exact sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] for $A\to K\to C\to A[1]$, the segment $\mathcal H^n(A)\to\mathcal H^n(K)\to\mathcal H^n(C)$ forces $\mathcal H^n(K)=0$ outside this interval. The triangle therefore lies in $D^b(Y,\Lambda)$, and its outer terms lie in the triangulated subcategory of [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory]. Hence $K\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ as required.
